note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 (independent judge, clean clone at c8584247bb) after a965d7c0d4 changed the cited producer responder_eap.go::handleResponderEAP. RFC 3748 Section 4: "Since EAP only defines Codes 1-4, EAP packets with other codes MUST be silently discarded by both authenticators and peers." The change adds CP payload collection to the inner-payload loop and, only when an AUTH payload is present and no CFG_REQUEST was decided yet, sets sa.cpRequest = decideCPRequest(cps); that branch then takes the AUTH-from-MSK path, which never reads the EAP payload. It sits after decryptAndParse and the eapMessageDiscarded early return, so a message carrying an EAP payload and no AUTH is handled exactly as before: sess.Process (eap.go) returns nil for Code 0 or above 4 before any state access, and handleResponderEAP returns at next == nil with no output. Peer Process (peer.go) and handleEAPResponse (fsm.go) are unchanged. The three tagged units are unchanged. TestEngineDiscardedEAPCodesPreserveExchange still sends encrypted Codes 0, 5 and 255 into both IKE roles through handleInbound, asserts state, expected Message ID, last sent message and retransmission deadline and count unchanged, then a held-back valid packet at the same Message ID advances each role and the exchange ends with matching nonzero MSKs and a verified AUTH. Discrimination records (whole-body reverts of the two Process functions) are current and prove reachability only; the handleEAPResponse result.Discarded return is held by the unchanged-state assertions. All three tagged tests and the core units pass at HEAD under -race.
